# R119.2 — Exact joint two-time S23 oracle with complexity controlled by the time difference

Date: 2026-11-13. Companion to R118's exact one-time integer-band lemma and R119.1's simultaneous-feasibility counterexample. Author-side auxiliary S23 ranked Boolean model. Frozen scientific-input pin remains 43ec6098b1330ae86d0a7863be336c5d97f6ef34, no repinning, no native Cell/Link/Port permission inference.

## Statement

Fix integers j,a,c,N,d with d nonzero and rational x. Existing old source eligibility signatures are constant on a rational point/open-gap partition of a compact rational interval I. Consider two newly introduced, *distinct* S23 times N and N+d. For each old atom, determine which **four joint Boolean pairs** (M_N(theta),M_(N+d)(theta)) are attained at one common theta, with exact rational witnesses, without enumerating either large-new-time collection of phase cuts.

**Theorem.** Refine each old open atom only at the integer crossings of the four affine phases

A=a theta, C=c theta, P=(a-d)theta, Q=(c-d)theta,

and of all six pairwise differences between these four phases. These extra cuts depend on a,c,d but not on N or x. On any refined open atom the four possible joint bits are each decided by at most four positive-width rational-affine integer-band checks of R118.1. Each attained bit pair has an exact rational witness in the same old atom. On old/new cut singleton atoms evaluate both original S23 predicates directly. Taking the union across refined atoms returns exactly all joint signatures for the two new times, even when old signature fibers are disconnected.

For q old atoms and r newly induced relative-phase cut points, at most 4(q+2r) joint-bit queries and 16(q+2r) integer-band checks suffice (conservative counts, counting every singleton). The number of relative cuts on a fixed rational interval of length Delta is O(1+Delta*(|a|+|c|+|d|)) with an absolute constant, regardless of |N|. Bit complexity additionally includes rational input length and log(|N|+2). For fixed d,a,c, query count is independent of the numerical magnitude of N. The old index, ranked history membership, signature storage and retained witnesses have their own costs.

## Proof: common-phase reduction

Put Z(theta)={x+(N-j)theta}. The later time satisfies

{x+(N+d-j)theta}={Z(theta)+d theta}.

For bit b=1 define E_b(theta) as the directed half-open circle arc from {a theta} to {c theta}; for b=0 define its complement, equivalently the opposite half-open arc when endpoints differ and the whole circle when they coincide. Translation by -d theta on the circle takes E_(b1)(theta) to the circular arc whose endpoints are {(a-d)theta} and {(c-d)theta}, or its complement. Thus the joint condition is exactly

Z(theta) in E_(b0)(theta) intersect (E_(b1)(theta)-d theta).

This identity is pointwise exact, including all half-open endpoint decisions and empty coincident-endpoint arcs.

## Proof: fixed-order segment intersection

On a refined open atom, the integer parts of A,C,P,Q and the order/equality of their fractional parts are constant, by the declared four-phase and six pairwise-difference cuts. In [0,1), each directed arc and each complement becomes a union of at most two half-open intervals [low(theta),up(theta)), with endpoints among 0,1,{A},{C},{P},{Q}. Every such endpoint is rational-affine on the refined atom. Intersecting one segment from the first set with one from the second yields [max(low0,low1),min(up0,up1)), or an empty interval. Since relative endpoint order is fixed, any nonempty intersection is a *strictly positive-width* interval on the whole open atom. Each arc has at most two segments, so the joint set has at most four candidate segment intersections.

On one such positive segment [L(theta),U(theta)), membership {x+(N-j)theta} in the segment is equivalent to existence of integer n satisfying

x+(N-j)theta-U(theta) < n <= x+(N-j)theta-L(theta).

These are the two rational-affine bounds of R118.1, so one constant-size exact arithmetic test decides feasibility and returns rational theta. A witness is verified against both original S23 predicates; singleton atoms are checked directly. This proves the theorem and retains complete old signatures and source identities when projected back to the old atoms. QED.

## Important scope

The theorem handles **two** new times with known integer difference d. It makes no assumption that the independently attainable bits form a Cartesian product (R119.1 explicitly disproves that). For large |d|, extra relative-phase cuts themselves may be numerous; the useful compression regime is small or otherwise compact d even when |N| is enormous. Expanding to three or more times requires additional relative-endpoint arrangements and careful control of the number of joint segments; this is not presumed automatic.

## Exact implementation verification

The separate checker check_r119_neighbor.py imports the exact R118.1 band primitive from the sibling R118 research folder (same branch). It uses Python Fraction and compares exact joint pair signatures to independently constructed **full six-phase atomizations for both new times** on 250 deterministic randomized bounded instances (seed 1192026). It additionally evaluates witnesses for four huge signed base times ±(10^80+7) and ±(10^150+19), with d=1, without enumerating their phase cuts.

Executed output: R119_NEIGHBOR_PASS.
Counters: 250 random instances; 6,734 old atoms; 8,078 relative-only refined atoms (including large cases); 32,312 joint-bit calls; 5,909 exact non-singleton joint witnesses; 12,386 full two-new-time brute atoms on bounded instances; maximum witness integer part bit length 999; four signed huge-base cases. All asserted comparisons passed. These finite checks are implementation evidence; the proof above establishes the all-integer one-pair theorem.

## Next frontier

For arbitrary separation d and multiple new times, construct a lattice/semilinear joint-feasibility oracle whose cost depends on input bit length and output signatures rather than explicitly on |d|; characterize when joint phase-order refinement must have Omega(|d|) components and when it can be compressed. Continue to preserve branch identity, signed phase semantics and exact half-open boundaries. Researcher activity and formal CLAIM/Result are separate Source records and remain subject to native control receipts.
